messages:
sarah: Heads-up — started canary rollout of NVIDIA 550.x to us-central GPU pool (~200 nodes). Seeing a small but obvious failure mode: ~6 nodes failed to finish provisioning and are dropped to initramfs with DKMS build errors. Attaching brief logs.
raj: Can you paste the dkms/journal tail? quick grep for UVM / nv-host errors helps.
provisioner-bot: [provision event] node-gn-078 failed provision step=dkms-build status=error code=MODULE_COMPILE timeout=1200s
sarah: logs: ```
Nov 12 05:12:01 node-gn-078 kernel: nvidia: module verification failed: signature and/or required key missing
Nov 12 05:12:03 node-gn-078 dkms: ERROR: Unable to build module nvidia-550 for kernel 6.1.0-197-generic (x86_64)
Nov 12 05:12:04 node-gn-078 modprobe: FATAL: Error inserting nvidia (Unknown symbol in module, or unknown parameter)
Nov 12 05:12:05 node-gn-078 systemd[1]: Started Load Kernel Modules.
Nov 12 05:12:06 node-gn-078 initramfs: UVM initialization failed: -22
```
Only partial set replicated here — full gist uploaded to S3: https://s3.redwood.internal/logs/2065001234-dkms-gist
mike: Saw similar on one canary earlier but attributed to mismatch with kernel-headers packaging after the distro security update. Did we change kernel ABI around the same time?
dina: We have two levers: 1) pin driver package to 535 on the canary pool and restart provisioning, or 2) enable `DKMS_BUILD_FLAGS="--force"` and collect full compile output for triage. For customer impact minimal, prefer rollback to 535 for now.
raj: Quick repro steps I used locally: flash small VM with kernel 6.1.0-197, apt-get install nvidia-driver-550, run `dkms autoinstall` -> see: ```
Error! Bad return status for module build on kernel: 6.1.0-197
Consult /var/lib/dkms/nvidia/550/build/make.log for more information.
```  make.log shows unresolved symbol refs in nvidia.uvm
provisioner-bot: node-gn-082 reported same FLOW: provision->dkms->timeout->rollback queued
sarah: Customer-facing pools unaffected so far, but provisioning backlog is starting to climb, CPU/GPU allocation waits + burst fills. We should stop further 550 rollouts immediately.
mike: Agree. I'll trigger a freeze and start rolling the canary back to 535. Note: we need to coordinate kernel-headers version across images — I saw one host with headers pinned to 6.1.0-195 and another to 6.1.0-197 which caused DKMS to pick wrong include paths.
dina: Command snippets for rollback (tested): ```
# mark hold and install 535 version
apt-get update && apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535
apt-mark hold nvidia-driver-535
systemctl reboot
```  
And for extra safety, disable automatic DKMS rebuild in provisioning by adding `ENV: DKMS_SKIP=1` to canary provisioner config.
raj: Also add `modprobe.blacklist=nvidia_drm` as a temporary test to see if initramfs can complete without the DRM path; helps in reproducing the failure boundary.
sarah: I'll open a rollback runbook and a paged alert for any new failed provisions. Schedule: stop rollouts now, start automated rollback in 10m, canary verify for 30m, then resume only after green.
ops-bot: [action] rollout-freeze applied to pool us-central-gpu by sarah at 2065001240
mike: Heads-up on capacity: rollback will free some canary nodes but will take ~8-12m per node to reprovision; expect ~12% reduction in available GPU capacity for the pool during the operation. Notify SRE and Capacity teams.
dina: I'll collect full dkms build logs from the failed nodes and run `strace` on the build in a sandbox. Also plan to test driver build with `--no-rebuild` kernel config to isolate header mismatch.
raj: If we confirm unresolved UVM symbols, likely an ABI change in 550 against our kernel packaging. We should open a vendor ticket and add a regression test in the provisioning CI that builds nvidia driver against each kernel-headers we ship.
sarah: Great. TL;DR: pause 550 canary, rollback to 535 on canary pool, collect full build logs, add CI test for dkms builds. I'll update status here in 20m. :thumbsup:
provisioner-bot: [note] repro count=3 nodes affected, queued for log collection
